Medieval Walnut Tart for the Feast of the Ass

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 45-55 min

The Feast of the Ass (Festum Asinorum) was a medieval Christian festival, often celebrated around the Christmas season or Epiphany, commemorating the Flight into Egypt. While not widely observed today, it was a joyous occasion. A rich, hearty walnut tart, made with seasonal ingredients, would have been a welcome and celebratory dessert at such a winter feast, offering warmth and sustenance.

Ingredients

  • For the Crust:
  • 1 1/4 cups (150 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 3-4 tablespoons (45-60 ml) ice water
  • For the Filling:
  • 1 1/2 cups (170 g) walnuts, roughly chopped
  • 3 large eggs
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) heavy cream
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon (optional)
  • Pinch of salt
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) honey or maple syrup (optional, for extra richness)

Method

  1. To make the crust: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. Cut in the cold, cubed butter using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining.
  2. Gradually add the ice water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Be careful not to overmix. Form the dough into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
  3. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough into a 12-inch (30 cm) circle. Carefully transfer the dough to a 9-inch (23 cm) tart pan with a removable bottom, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides.
  4. Trim any excess dough from the edges. Prick the bottom of the crust several times with a fork. Line the crust with parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes.
  5. Remove the pie weights and parchment paper, then continue to bake for another 5-7 minutes, or until the crust is lightly golden. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly while you prepare the filling.
  6. Reduce oven temperature to 350°F (175°C).
  7. To make the filling: In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, granulated sugar, melted butter, heavy cream, vanilla extract, cinnamon (if using), salt, and honey or maple syrup (if using) until well combined.
  8. Stir in the chopped walnuts.
  9. Pour the walnut filling into the pre-baked tart crust, spreading it evenly.
  10. Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the filling is set and golden brown. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean or with moist crumbs.
  11. Let the tart cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving. This allows the filling to fully set.

Tips

  • For an enhanced flavor, lightly toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 5-7 minutes before adding them to the filling.
  • Do not overwork the pastry dough; this will make it tough. Handle it as little as possible.
  • The tart can be served warm or at room temperature, and pairs wonderfully with a dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
